issues.body:
Section 4 states: 'Until a standards body assigns a namespace, `trustx:` denotes `https://w3id.org/sparq/trust-expression#`; these terms are non-standard proposal terms.' That binding is new and conflicts with two existing authorities.

(a) crates/sparq-trust/src/framework_vocab.rs:61 declares `TRUSTX_NS = "https://sparq.dev/ns/trust#"`, and its module doc says of the trustx: layer: 'it shares the same placeholder base IRI, https://sparq.dev/ns/trust#, since trustx: is a prose-only sub-prefix of trust: - not a distinct namespace'. That module is the shipped implementation of THIS program (its doc cites issue #1592 and research/trust-expression-spec.md).

(b) The companion published draft site/specs/trust-graph-authz.typ:170 declares `@prefix trustx: <https://sparq.dev/ns/trust#>`, and its own header comment says the Trust Expression draft 'owns the VERIFIER <-> HOLDER contract ... of the same trustx: vocabulary'.

Every term this draft declares normative already exists under the shipped IRI: TrustRequirements, question, trustsIssuer, trustsFramework, requiresScopeConformance, requiresValidStatusAt, methodPolicy, Framework, Certification, certifies, underFramework, scope, validFrom, validUntil, AnyServiceScope, StatusAttestation, coveredBy, eIDAS2, DIATF (framework_vocab.rs:74-144). Because RDF terms are identified by full IRI, an envelope authored per this draft shares zero terms with the shipped verifier and with the companion pod-side draft - the two halves of one program cannot interoperate. The design record's own D5 no-duplication rule (quoted in framework_vocab.rs:12) exists to prevent exactly this.
issues.fix_hint: Bind `trustx:` to `https://sparq.dev/ns/trust#` (matching framework_vocab.rs:61 and trust-graph-authz.typ:170) and reference crates/sparq-trust/src/framework_vocab.rs as the shipped constant surface for the section-6 vocabulary, rather than presenting it as newly minted inline. If a distinct namespace is genuinely intended, that is a breaking change to shipped code and a published draft, and must be justified explicitly in the draft and coordinated with framework_vocab.rs + trust-graph-authz.typ in the same change.
issues.title: Normative trustx: namespace contradicts the shipped vocabulary and the companion published draft

issues.body:
Section 6's normative table row reads: '[`trustx:validFrom`, `trustx:validUntil`], [Inclusive start and exclusive end of the certification validity interval.]'

The shipped implementation says the opposite for the end bound:
- crates/sparq-trust/src/framework_vocab.rs:117-120 documents BOTH bounds as '(inclusive)'.
- crates/sparq-trust/src/graph.rs:176: 'trustx:validUntil - inclusive end of the certification window (Unix seconds).'
- crates/sparq-trust/src/graph.rs:342: 'GATE 4 - TIME. The window must be well-formed AND cover `now` (inclusive).'

This is not a wording nit. For a certification (or, via the same properties, a StatusAttestation) whose validUntil is exactly the trustx:requiresValidStatusAt reference instant, a verifier conforming to this draft MUST reject while the shipped pod-side closure admits. In a document whose central premise is fail-closed, positive, time-windowed evidence, an inverted boundary at the expiry instant is a real admission divergence between the two halves of the program.

Related gap: [TX-STATUS-001] applies validFrom/validUntil to trustx:StatusAttestation and only says the interval 'covers the reference instant' - it never states the boundary convention at all, so status coverage is left undefined at exactly the instant that matters most.
issues.fix_hint: Change the table row to 'Inclusive start and inclusive end' to match framework_vocab.rs:117-120 and graph.rs:176/342 (or, if exclusive-end is a deliberate correction, change the shipped code in the same PR and say so). Separately, state the same boundary convention explicitly in [TX-STATUS-001] so status coverage is defined at the endpoints, and add the two endpoint cases (reference instant == validFrom, == validUntil) to the section 10 conformance-case list.
issues.title: Normative table declares trustx:validUntil an EXCLUSIVE end; the shipped closure implements it as INCLUSIVE

issues.body:
Section 4.3 states: '`trustx:eIDAS2` and `trustx:DIATF` SHOULD use `rdfs:seeAlso` to connect to the corresponding regulatory individuals vendored in `sparq_trust::secprop` rather than minting duplicate regulatory requirements.'

`sparq_trust::secprop` is the wrong ontology. Its module doc (crates/sparq-trust/src/secprop.rs:1-8) describes it as the security-PROPERTIES vocabulary under `https://w3id.org/zkp-sparql/sec-prop#` (Unlinkability, assurance levels, audit status), and at line 33 it says explicitly 'the full regulation->requirement chain is deliberately not modelled here'. Grepping crates/sparq-trust/src/secprop.rs for eIDAS or DIATF returns nothing.

The regulatory individuals actually live in the `sec-req:` namespace and are surfaced by framework_vocab.rs: `SEC_REQ_NS = "https://w3id.org/zkp-sparql/sec-req#"` (line 67), `SEC_REQ_EIDAS20 = ".../sec-req#Eidas20"` (line 149), plus the UK DVS individual; line 102 records the intended wiring - 'TRUSTX_EIDAS2 / TRUSTX_DIATF rdfs:seeAlso the vendored sec-req: ones'. So the draft's normative SHOULD directs implementers to a module that cannot satisfy it, and misses the module that already implements exactly this rule.
issues.fix_hint: Replace `sparq_trust::secprop` with the `sec-req:` regulatory-framework individuals surfaced by `sparq_trust::framework_vocab` (SEC_REQ_NS / SEC_REQ_EIDAS20 and the UK DVS constant, framework_vocab.rs:63-149). Note that sec-prop: (security properties) and sec-req: (regulatory requirements) are distinct vendored ontologies so the two are not confused again.
issues.title: [TX-MODE-FRAMEWORK] SHOULD points at sparq_trust::secprop, which contains no regulatory individuals

issues.body:
Section 6 opens 'The following terms and meanings are normative:' and then defines only seven entries (Framework, Certification, certifies, underFramework, scope, AnyServiceScope, validFrom/validUntil).

But MUST-level requirements elsewhere in the document depend on terms that section never defines: trustx:TrustRequirements, trustx:question, trustx:requiresValidStatusAt ([TX-REQ-002]); trustx:trustsIssuer ([TX-MODE-ENUM]); trustx:trustsFramework, trustx:requiresScopeConformance ([TX-MODE-FRAMEWORK]); trustx:StatusAttestation, trustx:credential, trustx:status, trustx:valid ([TX-STATUS-001]); trustx:coveredBy, trustx:underCertification ([TX-RESP-001]); trustx:methodPolicy ([TX-EVAL-003]). An implementer cannot build a conforming envelope or response from the normative text alone.

trustx:underCertification is a further problem: [TX-RESP-001] makes it mandatory for framework-mode responses, yet it appears in no table here and has no counterpart in the shipped constant set (framework_vocab.rs declares TRUSTX_COVERED_BY at line 135 but nothing for underCertification), so it is a newly minted term introduced only by example.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the section 6 table to cover every trustx: term the document requires normatively, or retitle the section to its actual scope and add a complete term index. For trustx:underCertification, either mint it deliberately (define it in the table and add the matching constant to crates/sparq-trust/src/framework_vocab.rs alongside TRUSTX_COVERED_BY) or express the certification link with an existing term.
issues.title: Section 6 is titled 'Normative certification-scope vocabulary' but omits most terms the document requires normatively

issues.body:
The 'Security standing' section and section 8 present `sparq_zk_compose::verifier::bind_issuer_attestations` and `sparq_zk_compose::verifier::bind_hidden_issuer_attestations` as the estate items an optional ZK realization 'builds on' and whose trusted issuer-key set is 'consumed by' them. Both are private: crates/sparq-zk-compose/src/verifier.rs:2739 and :3901 declare plain `fn`, not `pub fn`, and there is no re-export - outside the crate they are unreachable.

Section 7.3 likewise says 'RDF 1.2 triple-term parsing in the reference estate is provided by `sparq_core::nt::triple_term`'; crates/sparq-core/src/nt.rs:486 is also a private `fn`.

The surrounding statements are descriptive rather than conformance requirements, so this is not a soundness defect, but a spec that names module paths as integration anchors implies a callable surface that does not exist.
issues.fix_hint: Either name the public entry point that actually reaches these checks (e.g. the public verify/manifest-verification API in sparq-zk-compose that calls bind_issuer_attestations at verifier.rs:2647), or phrase the references as internal implementation anchors rather than integration points.
issues.title: Cited estate anchors are private items, not callable surface

issues.body: The [TX-STATUS-001] example block uses `prov:wasAttributedTo` but declares no `@prefix prov:` (prov: is first declared two sections later, in the section 7.1 block). The same block and the section 7.2 TriG block use `trustx:` and `ex:` without declaring them locally. Each example otherwise reads as a standalone, copy-pasteable snippet, so as written they will not parse on their own.
issues.fix_hint: Add the missing @prefix lines to each example block, or state once near the first example that a common prefix preamble is assumed throughout and give it explicitly.
issues.title: Turtle examples use prefixes they do not declare

verdict.summary:
Adds an Unofficial Proposal Draft (site/specs/trust-expression.typ) plus its registry entry. Mechanics are sound: the entry declares all seven single-line fields build-specs.mjs parses via parallel-array regexes; routes and e2e inventories are data-driven off SPECS so nothing breaks; every imported Typst helper exists in _lib/spec.typ; and both build-boundary honesty gates pass on the source (I ran check-no-perf-numbers.py --enforce and check-privacy-claims.sh: 0 findings). The sq-qhy4 and semi-honest-MPC caveats are stated plainly and repeatedly, and no perf numbers appear.

The problem is the normative content. The draft re-mints the trustx: vocabulary inline as if greenfield, but that vocabulary is ALREADY SHIPPED in crates/sparq-trust/src/framework_vocab.rs (whose doc cites this exact program, issue #1592) and already published in the companion draft site/specs/trust-graph-authz.typ. Two divergences are substantive: (1) the draft normatively binds trustx: to https://w3id.org/sparq/trust-expression#, while the implementation and the companion draft both use https://sparq.dev/ns/trust# and framework_vocab.rs states that trustx: is 'a prose-only sub-prefix of trust: - not a distinct namespace'; all ~19 terms declared normative here already exist at the other IRI, so a conforming envelope shares no terms with the shipped verifier; (2) the normative table declares validUntil an EXCLUSIVE end while framework_vocab.rs:120 and graph.rs:176/342 implement it as INCLUSIVE - an admission divergence at the exact expiry instant in a fail-closed decision. A third defect points a normative SHOULD at sparq_trust::secprop, the sec-prop: security-properties ontology, which holds no regulatory individuals; eIDAS2/UK-DVS live in sec-req: via framework_vocab.

No honesty-gate violation, but a normative spec that contradicts its own shipped implementation should not publish.
